subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: What Slack workspace, account, destination-access, and retention rules should govern a DM requester’s ability to query the agent’s own channel sends?
rationale: Current isolation is an intentional security boundary; source inspection proves the gap but cannot determine which cross-session disclosures are product-approved.

options.title: Scoped activity view
options.body: Persist canonical successful sends and authorize queries by agent, Slack workspace/account, and the requester’s destination access.

options.title: Broaden sibling access
options.body: Allow DM session tools to inspect sibling Slack sessions, accepting wider transcript disclosure and tighter coupling to session topology.

options.title: Keep strict isolation
options.body: Retain current boundaries and require explicit memory or targeted-session workflows for cross-context knowledge.

recommendation.title: Scoped activity view
recommendation.body: Persist canonical successful sends and authorize queries by agent, Slack workspace/account, and the requester’s destination access.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing, outbound, session-visibility, and prior decision history points to this person for the boundary choice.
